3.4.5.2 LdCom user generation
Similar to Com users, the LdCom user concept explained in document [17] supports a flexible number of callbacks with LdCom user specific LdCom user callback handle Ids. Those LdCom user callback handle Ids identify to which LdCom IPdu the notification belongs and are intended to directly index the Rte’s internal data structures. Like for the Com users, the LdComUserModuleCnf containers are intended to be setup manually by the integrator. This supports to statically configure the LdCom users with its LdComUserModule.LdComUserModuleCnfRef references in the LdCom module. Since the kind of notifications are strongly dependent from the features used by integrated SWCs and the RTE’s implementation strategy, it’s the task of the RTE Generator to create the configuration parameters underneath the LdComUserModuleCnf container.
[SWS_Rte_04631]{DRAFT} ⌈ If the external configuration switch strictConfigurationCheck (see [SWS_Rte_05148]) is set to false , the RTE Generator shall provide in the predefined LdComUserModuleCnf containers the required
• LdComUserIPdu container with LdComUserCbkHandleId, LdComUserSystemTemplateSignalRef and LdComUserCallbackRefs AND
• LdComUserCallback with LdComUserCallbackName and LdComUserCallbackType AND
• LdComUserHeaderInclude according its internal implementation requirements.
⌋()
[SWS_Rte_04635]{DRAFT} ⌈ If the external configuration switch strictConfigurationCheck (see [SWS_Rte_05150]) is set to true, and the input of the RTE generator contains an RTE configuration which references a LdComUserIPdu with no defined LdComUserCbkHandleId in the provided LdCom configuration, the RTE generator shall reject this input as invalid configuration.⌋()
[SWS_Rte_04636]{DRAFT} ⌈If the external configuration switch strictConfigurationCheck (see [SWS_Rte_05150]) is set to true, the RTE generator shall reject configurations violating the [SWS_LdCom_CONSTR_00009], [SWS_LdCom_CONSTR_- 00010] or [SWS_LdCom_CONSTR_00011].⌋()
